family.description: This entry represents the N-terminal of dermatan-sulfate epimerase (DSE) from mammals, and heparin-sulfate lyase (HepB) from bacteria [[cite:PUB00076523]]. DSE converts D-glucuronic acid to L-iduronic acid (IdoUA) residues. It plays an important role in the biosynthesis of the glycosaminoglycan/mucopolysaccharide dermatan sulfate [[cite:PUB00162452],[cite:PUB00109125]]. HepB cleaves both heparin and heparan sulfate glycosaminoglycans through a beta-elimination mechanism. It cleaves heparin at alpha-D-GlcNp2S6S(1->4) alpha-L-IdoAp2S and heparan sulfate at alpha-D-GlcNp2Ac(or 2S)6OH(1->4)beta-D-GlcAp [[cite:PUB00016410]]. This domain is composed of helical hairpins.
family.name: Dermatan-sulfate epimerase-like, N-terminal
